payload.text: OPTIMIZE: Please split monolithic files into separate files. In particular, look into splitting out Tutorial functionality. As I continue adding Tutorial lessons, I'm hitting snags where things like the UI and the game board are being broken as the agent tries to implement them. By splitting these out, I hope to minimize the chances that those areas of code get touched when adding and editing tutorial-related code.

**Analyzing Tutorial Components**

I'm currently focused on dissecting the `utils.ts` file within the Tutorial functionality. I'm aiming to pinpoint the key areas contributing to its monolithic nature. My priority is preventing future UI and game logic regressions as we integrate new lessons, so I'm paying close attention to component responsibilities and dependencies.


**Defining Data Organization**

I've decided to tackle the tutorial data next. The goal is to separate lesson definitions from the core game logic. Specifically, I plan to move tutorial steps and lessons into their own directory under `data/tutorial`. I'll put tutorial-specific helper functions, like deck creation, into `utils/tutorialUtils.ts`.


**Prioritizing UI Decomposition**

I'm now shifting my focus toward `App.tsx` and UI component extraction, after clarifying the user request. My primary goal is to carve out specific game area components. I will start by separating `GameBoard.tsx`, `PlayerZone.tsx`, and modals from the monolithic `App.tsx`. I believe this will provide a substantial improvement to modularity and maintainability. I will use the established tutorial refactor as a guide for these component splits.


**Refactoring Utility Modules**

I'm now diving into the `utils` directory. I'm removing tutorial constants and moving the CPU logic to `ai/cpu.ts`. I'll create `utils/tutorial.ts` for tutorial-specific helpers and data, and `utils/deck.ts` for deck-related functions. General game utilities will go in `utils/game.ts`. The original `utils.ts` will stay, and serve as a barrel file.

**Reorganizing App Logic**

I am now focused on cleaning up tutorial logic in `App.tsx`. I will be working to extract the tutorial-specific overrides in `handleCardClick` and abstracting the "Is Interaction Allowed" check into a separate hook or utility function, imported from a new file. Tutorial data will also be moved out to clean up imports.


**Structuring Utility Imports**

I'm now restructuring my imports, focusing on the `utils` directory. I'm creating `utils/core.ts` for generic helpers (`generateId`, `shuffle`). I'll also add `utils/deck.ts` for card-related functions, `utils/gameLogic.ts` for rule-related logic, and `utils/cpu.ts` for AI. The tutorial data will be in `data/tutorials.ts`. Finally, I'll update the original `utils.ts` to re-export the new files to maintain import compatibility.


**Defining Component Architecture**

I'm now zeroing in on the architecture of the `App.tsx` split. While my initial inclination was to extract a `PlayerArea` component, the mobile/desktop rendering variations complicate a clean separation. I'm leaning toward creating `components/game/PlayerBoard.tsx`, which renders the Field, Resources, and Hand for a specific player. This encapsulates the visual duplication. I recognize that there are complicating issues with this component, however.


**Refining Utility Functions**

I'm now revising the plan for utility functions. I'll focus on separating specific card-related logic into `utils/cards.ts`, including functions like `createDeck` and tutorial-specific deck creation. I'll also centralize rule-based logic to `utils/rules.ts`, and AI logic into `utils/ai.ts`. `data/tutorials.ts` will hold the lesson definitions, and the original `utils.ts` will be removed. I'll delete it and update imports to point to specific files.


**Implementing File Architecture**

I'm now implementing the planned file structure for utilities and data. The directory structure is solidified, as planned, and the files above have been populated with the specified functions and imports. I've also moved the game modals into `components/modals/GameModals.tsx`. The goal is to finish the restructuring of the project. I'm now making final updates to `App.tsx` imports and reducing its size.


**Defining Component Layout**

I am now focusing on restructuring the game board view. I am leaning toward a `PlayerArea` component, which will handle the Field, Resources, and Hand. However, the UI layout differs substantially between mobile and desktop versions. So, I will proceed with creating a `PlayerArea` component that takes `player`, `isTop`, and `interactionHandlers` as props, and I will refactor `App.tsx` and move all the modals into their own files. I am working to define a file and component architecture that can support responsive rendering.


**Updating Component Extraction**

I'm now prioritizing the separation of the data and logic. My current focus is to move `TUTORIAL_LESSONS`, and the related helper functions, to `data/tutorials.ts`. Dependencies include `createDeck` and `createTutorialCard`, so I'll ensure that `data/tutorials.ts` imports from `utils/cards.ts`. I'm working to remove all references to these variables from `App.tsx`. I've also moved `LogEntry` to a dedicated UI component.


**Defining File Structure**

I'm now in the file creation and update phase. I've established the new directory structure, creating `utils/core.ts`, `utils/cards.ts`, `utils/rules.ts`, `utils/ai.ts`, `data/tutorials.ts`, `components/modals/GameModals.tsx`, `components/modals/DiscardModal.tsx`, and `components/ui/LogEntry.tsx`. I'm starting to update `App.tsx` by moving modals and `LogEntry` to their own files and updating all imports to the new file structure. The original `utils.ts` will be retained as a barrel file.
